events.what: Karpenkov's sin^2-algorithm settles the totally-real cubic case (n=3)

Tagnon's deterministic sin^2-type algorithm for complex (signature (1,1)) cubics, with periodicity certificates on 205 sampled polynomials, a [-3,3]^3 box search (194/194), and one Lean-checked field; companion arXiv:2608.24750 proves finiteness/descent lemmas
events.ai_basis: This research was AI-assisted. All computations were carried out under a fixed audit protocol ... adversarial review of the manuscript itself ... the human author directed the work

judgement.doubts: The record says the paper's own abstract states 'The general periodicity problem remains open' and that the evidence is certificates on 205 sampled cubics plus a finite box search and a single Lean instance — finitely many instances, the example F4 names. If the companion paper's finiteness/descent theorems in fact amount to a general termination proof for all (1,1) cubics, this would become a case (partial); the record does not say so. Even then it would be a case of n=3 only, never whole. The AI disclosure is vague; ai_role none is kept for the record, though it doesn't affect the status now.

corrections.why: F4/F1: the record's own summary says the paper verifies periodicity on '205 sampled complex cubic polynomials plus an exhaustive search over [-3,3]^3', with a single Lean-checked field, 'rather than a general proof that the algorithm terminates for all (1,1) cubics', and that the abstract says 'The general periodicity problem remains open'. That makes it scope instances, which is discarded. Even as a full proof it would be a case of n=3 (partial), not claimed. Karpenkov's totally-real case predates the snapshot and is a partial result, not a resolution, so the status is open, not open_stale.
F14: the status is open, so the direction must be null (§4 step 6).
